newsitem.title: UK: Britain probes apparent ammunition loss in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Britain probes apparent ammunition loss in Bosnia.

text.p: Military police are to investigate the apparent disappearance of $6 million worth of ammunition sent to Britain's peacekeeping forces in former Yugoslavia, a top government official said on Monday.

Richard Mottram, the defence ministry's senior civil servant, told parliament's Public Accounts Committee that some 3.9 million pounds' worth of ammunition which documents showed had gone to British bases in Bosnia could not be traced.
"We have decided to set in hand an inquiry by the special investigations branch of the Royal Military Police," said Mottram, the ministry's permanent undersecretary.

Asked by a legislator whether he could say the ammunition had not been stolen, he added: "I have no evidence that it has fallen into the wrong hands, but until we have carried out this investigation, I cannot give you that assurance."

A report published last month by Britain's National Audit Office said that in October last year, the total ammunition stock held by the British contingent of Bosnia's international peace implementation force was worth 55.5 million pounds.

It revealed that the British forces, which at one stage totalled 11,500, had run into considerable problems in accounting for their equipment, with records showing 452 anti-tank missiles in one store where none ever existed.
Mottram said the ministry had been trying to enforce the sort of accounting standards normal in a peacetime situation in a place where military operations were difficult and dangerous.
